messages:
alex_w: Heads-up: PR #18390 CI microbench failed — kv warmprefetch path shows ~8% tail latency regression vs golden. Marking this as a potential rollout blocker.
ci-bot: [CI] bench/micro/kv_prefetch failed on job linux-x86-18390. summary: baseline=1.02ms new=1.11ms diff=+8.8% (threshold=+5%). logs: https://ci.redwood/18390/bench.log
jamie: link to bench.log? can you paste the hotlines / sample flame?
alex_w: pasted snippet from bench.log:
```
bench: seq=32 batch=8
kv_hit_rate: 99.1% -> 94.3%
kernel_selector: selected quant-cuda (latency 1.11ms) vs fp16-opt (1.02ms)
stack: runtime::autoselect -> batcher::coalesce -> kv::warmpath
```
looks like kernel autoselect preferred a different kernel when the prefetch path is hot.
tony_g: that smells like the autoselect heuristic change from runtime PR 18270 (affinity + quant heuristics). did 18390 touch that?
mike: 18390 is actually a model-pack change but CI picked a different kernel due to slightly different seq/batch shape. bisect plan: run `git bisect` between last-green (commit 7a1f3) and HEAD-of-merge, but we should also run microbench locally with `./tools/bench --kv-prefetch --repeat 50`. I can run the bisect.
sara_p: I repro'd locally with docker + perf. Tail latency only spikes when kv warmpath hit drops below ~96% hit-rate. Increasing batch coalescer window made it worse (more coalescing -> different seq shapes).
jamie: can you try forcing kernel via env to confirm? `RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL=fp16-opt ./tools/bench --kv-prefetch`
sara_p: did that — forcing fp16-opt restores baseline numbers locally (1.03ms). So autoselect picked quant-cuda incorrectly for this workload.
ci-bot: [debug-run] bench/micro/kv_prefetch (debug) baseline=1.02ms new=1.05ms diff=+3.0% -- debug config: RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL=fp16-opt, kv_prefetch_window=32. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/18390/debug/bench-debug.log
linda_ops: quick Q: is this impacting Dedicated customers or Hosted only? any SLA exposure?
alex_w: looks limited to the specific kernel+batch shape — we haven't seen customer incidents yet, but it's risky for canaries. marking as rollout-blocker for this release cycle. :warning:
mike: update: bisect found probable culprit commit 0ab9cdef — allocator affinity tweak + quant affinity heuristic tweak introduced in PR 18270. reverting that commit locally fixes autoselect choice.
jamie: can we do a smaller hotfix: bias autoselect to prefer fp16-opt for sequence <=64 and kv_prefetch_enabled=true? less risky than full revert.
alex_w: good idea. I'll open two PRs: 1) revert 0ab9cdef as emergency revert (PR 18396), 2) follow-up config bias PR to harden the autoselect thresholds. Will run canary once revert merges.
sara_p: also adding a golden microbench that asserts kv_hit_rate >= 98.5% for warmprefetch on our CI image so this drops into red on PRs.
jamie: yes please add that to the microbench suite and threshold diffs so future autoselect changes fail CI fast.
ci-bot: scheduled canary run for PR 18396 on canary-prod (3 nodes) — results expected in ~15m.
mike: I'll monitor and if canary is green I'll coordinate a quick rollback rollout. starting revert PR now.
alex_w: thanks team. assigning follow-ups: mike = bisect/revert, jamie = CI golden test, sara_p = repro steps + docs, linda_ops = customer impact msg if canary shows regressions.
jamie: ack.
alex_w: tagging this thread as blocker until revert CI passes. :heavy_exclamation_mark:
